unlock_condition.description: Available early but the player needs funds to benefit from it

tile_details.description: very old worn stone paths, some cracked and uneven — older than any other city in the game
Egyptian-influenced decorative friezes carved into building facades near the trade row
papyrus rolls visible through open windows, ink stains on doorsteps
at the northwest corner, old stone foundations of pre-Phoenician buildings stick out of the ground

night.note: Quieter and darker at night than Sidon or Tyre — this is an older, slower city

location.lore_note: Byblos is the oldest city in the game world. It has been trading with Egypt for over a thousand years before the game begins. The word 'Bible' comes from Byblos — papyrus scrolls were so associated with this city that the Greeks named books after it. The city feels wise, ancient, and slightly mysterious. It moves slower than Tyre or Sidon.

visual.description: The oldest functioning harbor in the game. Stone quays worn smooth by a thousand years of ships. Egyptian hieroglyphs carved into the dock pillars.

services.note: Called a 'tithe' here rather than a fee — paid to the temple, not a harbor master

visual.description: A wide low building with an open courtyard. Scribes work at stone tables. Shelves of papyrus rolls line every wall from floor to ceiling. Smells of ink and dry papyrus.

inventory.note: Worth far more in Egypt and Greece than in Byblos — a major early arbitrage item

special_service.description: Player can bring unknown inscriptions found in ruins to be translated here. Costs silver, reveals lore.

visual.description: Run by an Egyptian merchant family that has lived in Byblos for three generations. The building mixes Phoenician stone construction with Egyptian decorative elements — painted walls, lotus column tops.

inventory.note: Used in Egyptian embalming and glass-making. High value in Sidon's glass quarter.

visual.description: An open yard near the harbor stacked with cut cedar logs and planks. Workers measure and sort by quality. The smell of cedar is overwhelming and pleasant.

buildings.note: Byblos cedar is slightly cheaper than Tyre cedar — the forest is closer. Best place to stock up on cedar before heading to Egypt where it is worth significantly more.

lines.speaker: shipitbaal
lines.text: Don't touch anything. These scrolls are older than your village. Older than most villages.

lines.speaker: shipitbaal
lines.text: Are you buying, or do you have something interesting for me?

player_choices.text: I found some old carvings I cannot read

lines.speaker: shipitbaal
lines.text: Byblos was old when Egypt was young. We gave the world the alphabet. We gave the world papyrus trade. And what did the world give us back? Merchant fees and bad weather.

secret.description: Possesses a scroll describing a voyage made by an unknown sailor 400 years ago — the earliest written account of something beyond the Pillars. He will not sell it. He might share it.

lines.speaker: amenhotep
lines.text: A Phoenician from the villages. My family has been here three generations and we still get called foreigners. You will too, one day, somewhere.

lines.speaker: amenhotep
lines.text: Trade well and I will introduce you to my cousin in Memphis. He runs the docks on the Nile.

entry_position.description: A collapsed section of flooring at the ruins edge — looks like rubble but leads down

discovery_triggers.description: Shipitbaal mentions ancient tunnels under the old quarter during lore dialogue
Player notices a hollow sound when walking near a certain rubble pile

options.description: Use any tool to clear enough rubble to enter

contents.description: A complete small temple predating Phoenician Byblos. Altar intact. Offerings of objects no one can identify.
Ancient offering objects on the altar — bronze, bone, and a material that looks like amber but isn't
Full wall inscription in the same unknown writing from Tyre's Drowned Quarter
contents.note: If player already has the tablet_rubbing from Tyre, this triggers a revelation: same civilization wrote both

reward_summary.connection_to_tyre: Same unknown writing as Tyre's Drowned Quarter — seeds a larger mystery across locations

steps.description: Return after 3 days for the translation
Shipitbaal can only partially translate — it is older than any writing he knows. He needs a matching inscription to compare.

steps.location_hint: ruins somewhere along the Phoenician coast

reward.note: Reveals that the unknown writing appears in multiple locations — and that whoever wrote it knew about the western ocean

steps.description: Amenhotep's cousin at the Memphis docks

reward.note: Unlocks reduced docking fees in Memphis and a trade contact there

economy.note: Byblos is the knowledge hub of the game — scrolls, maps, and translations are cheaper and more available here than anywhere else. Cedar is also at its cheapest here.
